_comment: Single source of truth for release packaging, the web flasher and the CLI. Keys are PlatformIO env names. mcu/radio/display/extras/status are what the board matrix in docs/hardware.md shows; tools/board_docs.py renders it from here.
_local_link: Per-board host connectivity, read by tools/board_caps.py into BOARD_* build flags and by the settings API. usb.native = the MCU's own D+/D- reach the connector; usb.ncm/cdc_acm = the silicon could present those classes there (whether this firmware build does is HAS_USB_NCM, derived in Config.h); usb.auto_reset_dtr_rts = esptool can reset the chip through this port without BOOT being held; uart.network = the UART behind the bridge carries PPP (HAS_PPP follows it: the node is the PPP client, the host's pppd the server — docs/local-link.md); uart.instance = which UART the bridge sits on; uart.qualification = the speeds PPP may be set to, ascending, 115200 among them; uart.tested_max_baud = the highest of those actually run on the hardware — the firmware refuses anything faster, so raise it only after trying it; rts/cts = flow-control lines the bridge exposes to the chip (none do).

_usb_identity._comment: What the S3's composite USB device (CDC-ACM console + CDC-NCM network) says it is; the ACM interface itself is the core's and named by it. tools/board_caps.py hands the strings to the core as USB_MANUFACTURER/USB_PRODUCT/USB_NETWORK_INTERFACE and the pair to the firmware as RETIMESH_USB_VID/RETIMESH_USB_PID (the core's variant header fixes USB_VID/USB_PID, so UsbNcm.cpp supplies the device descriptor itself); the host tool recognises the pair and the product string; the serial number is the factory MAC. 1209:0001 is pid.codes' test allocation, permitted for development and forbidden for anything shipped; an Espressif PID under 0x303A is requested per github.com/espressif/usb-pids.

t3s3.name: LilyGO T3-S3 v1.2/v1.3 (SX1262 or SX1276/78)
t3s3.notes: 0.96" OLED, 4 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM. The transceiver (SX1262 or SX1276/78) is detected at boot. Native USB — hold BOOT while pressing RST if the port is not detected.

esp32s3-qspi.name: Generic ESP32-S3 DevKitC-1 + SX1262 module
esp32s3-qspi.notes: 8 MB flash, quad PSRAM. Wire the SX1262 as documented in platformio.ini (PIN_LORA_* overrides).

tbeam.name: LilyGO T-Beam v1.1/v1.2 (SX1276 or SX1262)
tbeam.extras: 18650 holder, AXP192/AXP2101 PMU, u-blox GPS, PPP over the CH9102 bridge; **no SD slot**
tbeam.status: verified on hardware — see the T-Beam notes below; PPP built, not yet run on this board
tbeam.notes: 18650 holder, AXP192/AXP2101 power management, u-blox GPS, 0.96" OLED, no SD card slot. The transceiver and the PMU revision are both detected at boot. Serial is a CH9102 bridge — hold the middle button while pressing RST if flashing does not start. The serial port also carries PPP: pppd on the host makes the node a network interface at 10.65.<n>.1 (docs/local-link.md).

t3s3-sx1280.name: LilyGO T3-S3 with SX1280 (2.4 GHz)
t3s3-sx1280.notes: 0.96" OLED, SD slot, 4 MB flash. The plain SX1280 module: no power amplifier, so the chip's 13 dBm ceiling applies. The amplified variant is a different image — see t3s3-sx1280-pa. The radio is selected at build time rather than detected, so neither is interchangeable with the sub-GHz t3s3 build. Defaults to 2445 MHz / 812.5 kHz / SF8.

t3s3-sx1280-pa.name: LilyGO T3-S3 with SX1280 + PA (2.4 GHz)
t3s3-sx1280-pa.status: **builds only — never run on hardware**, see below
t3s3-sx1280-pa.notes: As t3s3-sx1280, but for the amplified module: the PA sits behind an RX/TX switch on GPIO 21/10 and the ceiling rises to 20 dBm. Flashing this image on a plain board would drive two GPIOs that board uses for something else, so pick by what is actually fitted.

heltec-ws.name: Heltec Wireless Stick V2/V2.1
heltec-ws.extras: PPP over the CP2102 bridge (no SD, no GNSS)
heltec-ws.status: verified on hardware; PPP built, not yet run on this board
heltec-ws.notes: 0.49" 64x32 OLED on the switched Vext rail, SX1276, 8 MB flash, no SD slot and no GNSS. The small panel gets its own page layout — ten columns and four rows — rather than the 128x64 one clipped. Serial is a CP2102 bridge, and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. The serial port also carries PPP: pppd on the host makes the node a network interface at 10.65.<n>.1 (docs/local-link.md). Uses the 8 MB partition table for the same reason the V3 does: no SD card, so the filesystem is the only storage the transport store has.

heltec-wb.name: Heltec Wireless Bridge
heltec-wb.extras: front LEDs for Wi-Fi and LoRa (the BLE one stays dark), aluminium shell, two SMA sockets, internal 2-pin battery connector, PPP over the CP2102 bridge; no SD, no GNSS
heltec-wb.status: verified on hardware; PPP built, not yet run on this board
heltec-wb.notes: The Wireless Stick's ESP32 and SX1276 in an aluminium box with two SMA antenna sockets, 8 MB flash and 8 MB PSRAM, no display, no SD slot and no GNSS: a headless relay. Serial is a CP2102 bridge on the micro-USB socket, and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. The serial port also carries PPP: pppd on the host makes the node a network interface at 10.65.<n>.1 (docs/local-link.md) — the one IP link a headless box in a cupboard has besides Wi-Fi. Uses the 8 MB partition table: no SD card, so the filesystem is the only storage the transport store has.

heltec-v3.name: Heltec WiFi LoRa 32 V3
heltec-v3.radio: SX1262 (TCXO, DIO2 drives the RF switch)
heltec-v3.display: 0.96" SSD1306 on the switched Vext rail
heltec-v3.extras: PPP over the CP2102 bridge (no SD, no GNSS)
heltec-v3.status: verified on hardware; PPP built, not yet run on this board
heltec-v3.notes: 0.96" 128x64 OLED on the switched Vext rail, SX1262 with a TCXO, 8 MB flash and no PSRAM, no SD slot and no GNSS. Very common hardware. A CP2102 bridge rather than the S3's native USB, so it appears as /dev/ttyUSB* and not as an Espressif JTAG device — and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. The serial port also carries PPP: pppd on the host makes the node a network interface at 10.65.<n>.1 (docs/local-link.md), and being an S3 it can be put into its downloader over that link. Uses an 8 MB partition table: the stock one maps only the first 4 MB, and with no SD card the filesystem is the only storage the transport store has.

heltec-wp.name: Heltec Wireless Paper
heltec-wp.radio: SX1262 (TCXO, DIO2 drives the RF switch)
heltec-wp.extras: PPP over the CP2102 bridge (no SD, no GNSS)
heltec-wp.status: verified on hardware (console, Wi-Fi, transport, SX1262 self-test, e-paper panel); PPP built, not yet run on this board
heltec-wp.notes: The WiFi LoRa 32 V3's ESP32-S3 and SX1262 with a 2.13" e-ink panel in place of the OLED, 8 MB flash and no PSRAM, no SD slot and no GNSS. The panel is driven through the display abstraction: pages draw on a GFX canvas and a refresh policy decides what reaches the glass, because an e-ink screen is written in whole frames and takes most of a second to do it. Revisions differ only in the panel — V1.0 is a DEPG0213BNS800, V1.1 an LCMEN2R13EFC1, V1.1.1 and V1.2 an E0213A367 — while the pins are the same across all of them; this build drives the E0213A367, so it covers V1.1.1 and V1.2. A CP2102 bridge rather than the S3's native USB, so it appears as /dev/ttyUSB* and not as an Espressif JTAG device — and every CP2102 reports the serial number 0001, so with more than one attached /dev/serial/by-id/ names only one of them and the rest have to be found by path. The serial port also carries PPP, as on the other Heltec boards. The radio's reset, busy and IRQ pins are the Heltec S3 family's rather than sourced twice for this board, so it boots with the radio self-test on — which passed on the first flash, one packet out and one back, and is what settles them.

heltec-v4.name: Heltec V4 (TFT)
heltec-v4.mcu: ESP32-S3: 16 MB flash, 2 MB PSRAM in package
heltec-v4.radio: SX1262 (TCXO, DIO2 drives the RF switch) behind a GC1109 or KCT8103L front end
heltec-v4.display: 2.4" 240x320 ST7789 with a CHSC6X touch layer
heltec-v4.extras: two buttons, piezo sounder, battery ADC, GNSS on the expansion header (no SD)
heltec-v4.status: builds; NOT verified on hardware — no pin below has been run
heltec-v4.notes: The first colour panel and the first amplified front end in this firmware, and the first 16 MB board. The pin map has one published source — the board definition in the open-source firmware it ships with (variants/esp32s3/heltec_v4, the TFT build) — rather than the two this project prefers, so the panel, touch, button and sounder pins are unverified; the LoRa pins are the V3's and carry more weight. The front end is the part with no equivalent elsewhere here: the radio is deaf and mute until the amplifier rail is powered and its mode pins are driven, and which of two parts is fitted is read off GPIO 2 at boot. Native USB, so it enumerates as an Espressif JTAG/serial device with its MAC in the by-id name and none of the CP2102 ambiguity the rest of this bench has. OTG and NCM are untested and left off.
